This review summarizes the current knowledge on immunological barriers in lung xenotransplantation, including mechanisms of hyperacute, delayed, and chronic rejection. seleccion.titulo: H3-K27M mutation alters the dynamics of human hematopoietic stem cells and delays erythroid differentiation

Los hallazgos contribuyen a entender mecanismos de leucemogénesis temprana con potencial traslacional terapéutico.

Among these, the histone H3-K27M mutation, originally identified in pediatric high-grade gliomas, reshapes gene repression programs by reducing global H3-K27 trimethylation. Although rare, H3-K27M mutations have been detected in preleukemic hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) of AML patients, suggesting its role in early leukemogenesis and identifying it as a promising therapeutic target. seleccion.titulo: Dead, frozen and revived: how xenotransplantation can contribute to species conservation
seleccion.resumen_previo: Investigación innovadora que combina vitrificación de tejidos y xenotrasplante en ratones inmunodeficientes para revitalizar material genético de jaguares comprometido por degradación post-mortem. El enfoque demuestra la aplicación de técnicas de xenotrasplante para conservación de especies amenazadas.

Rescuing high-quality genetic material from vehicular casualties is often limited by the prolonged post-mortem interval (PMI), which leads to advanced tissue degradation. This study evaluates an innovative pipeline combining solid-surface vitrification and xenotransplantation into immunodeficient mice to revitalize compromised jaguar tissues. seleccion.titulo: C‐Reactive Protein as a Biomarker of Inflammation and Graft Injury After Kidney and Heart Allo‐ and Xenotransplantation Into Non‐Human Primates
seleccion.resumen_previo: Publicación en revista especializada evaluando la proteína C reactiva como biomarcador de inflamación y daño de injerto en modelos primates de xenotrasplantes renales y cardíacos. El estudio compara la sensibilidad de CRP para detectar rechazo agudo específico del injerto entre diferentes especies de primates.

We evaluated CRP alongside tissue injury markers in non‐human primate (NHP) models of kidney and heart allo‐ and xeno‐transplantation to assess CRP's sensitivity in detecting graft‐specific inflammatory responses (acute rejection), and explored CRP elevations in the absence of clinically evident graft injury. A secondary objective compared CRP dynamics between NHP species. However, orthotopic pig-to-human liver xenotransplantation remained a challenge owing to the liver immunological and physiological complexity. Here we report the orthotopic pig-to-human liver xenotransplantation in a brain-deceased individual. seleccion.titulo: Artificial intelligence in preclinical nonhuman primate xenotransplantation: bridging the gap from data complexity to clinical precision
seleccion.resumen_previo: Propone el uso de inteligencia artificial y machine learning para interpretar la complejidad de datos generados en modelos preclínicos de xenotrasplante en primates no humanos, con aplicaciones en fenotipaje comportamental, detección temprana de rechazo y simulación de mellizos digitales. El enfoque aborda un cuello de botella metodológico relevante para la traslación clínica.

Este relevamiento de actitudes en población general constituye información de política pública valiosa ante el avance inminente de estas terapias.

seleccion.titulo: Histo-anatomical atlas of Garra rufa and its thermal tolerance at human body temperature
seleccion.resumen_previo: Se describe el análisis histo-anatómico de Garra rufa y su tolerancia térmica a 37°C, con potencial como modelo animal para xenotrasplante de cáncer humano e investigación de enfermedades infecciosas. Aunque es investigación biológica novedosa, el vínculo con xenotrasplante es secundario.
seleccion.extracto: Garra rufa, the doctor fish, is a small freshwater cyprinid notable for its exceptional tolerance to high temperatures, surviving at the human body temperature of 37 °C, and has emerging potential as a novel laboratory model for human cancer xenotransplantation and infectious disease research.
